When SD_PREFER_SIBLING is set on a sched domain
only if the local group has extra capacity. The extra check prevents the case
where you always pull from the heaviest group when it is already under-utilized
(possible with a large weight task outweighs the tasks on the system).
For example
column2: consider a 16-cpu quad-core quad-socket machine with MC and NUMA

column1: scheduling domains. Let's say we spawn 15 nice0 tasks and one nice-15 task
and each task is running on one core. In this case
events when balancing at the NUMA domain:
- find_busiest_group() will always pick the sched group containing the niced
task to be the busiest group.
- find_busiest_queue() will then always pick one of the cpus running the
nice0 task (never picks the cpu with the nice -15 task since
weighted_cpuload > imbalance).
- The load balancer fails to migrate the task since it is the running task
and increments sd->nr_balance_failed.
- It repeats the above steps a few more times until sd->nr_balance_failed > 5
at which point it kicks off the active load balancer
thread and kicks the nice 0 task off the cpu.
The load balancer doesn't stop until we kick out all nice 0 tasks from
the sched group
column2: leaving you with 3 idle cpus and one cpu running the

column1: nice -15 task.
When balancing at the NUMA domain
column2: we drop sgs.group_capacity to 1 if the child

column1: domain (in this case MC) has SD_PREFER_SIBLING set.  Subsequent load checks are
not relevant because the niced task has a very large weight.
In this patch
column2: we add an extra condition to the ""if(prefer_sibling)"" check in

column1: update_sd_lb_stats(). We drop the capacity of a group only if the local group
has extra capacity
column2: ie. nr_running < group_capacity. This patch preserves the

column1: original intent of the prefer_siblings check (to spread tasks across the system
in low utilization scenarios) and fixes the case above.
It helps in the following ways:
- In low utilization cases (where nr_tasks << nr_cpus)
group_capacity down to 1 if we prefer siblings.
- On very busy systems (where nr_tasks >> nr_cpus)
likely be > sgs.group_capacity.
- When balancing large weight tasks
column2: if the local group does not have extra

column1: capacity
column2: we do not pick the group with the niced task as the busiest group.

column1: This prevents failed balances
